story_ideas.headline: The home health rule changes which visits Medicare pays for next year
story_ideas.angle: A plain reading of the 11/09/26 final rule's temporary behavior adjustment, recalibrated case-mix weights and low-utilization policy, for families receiving home health and the agencies billing for it.
story_ideas.hook: This is a final rule, not a proposal, published 11/09/26 and setting CY 2027 home health payment.

story_ideas.b2b: Agencies have weeks to model the recalibrated case-mix weights, comorbidity subgroups and the finalized temporary behavior adjustment against next year's census and staffing plan.

story_ideas.title: Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program and Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program
story_ideas.headline: Drug price negotiation stops being a law and becomes a rulebook
story_ideas.angle: What the 11/09/26 final rule codifies about the negotiation program, Part D policy and fixed-combination drugs that are new formulations, written for people filling prescriptions under Part D.
story_ideas.hook: The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 authority is now finalized and codified in regulation rather than left to guidance.
story_ideas.consumer: Pull your current Part D drug list and check which of your medications are fixed combination products, because the rule finalizes a specific policy for new formulations of those.
story_ideas.b2b: Plans and pharmacy operations teams need the codified Part D policies mapped before 2027 benefit administration locks.

The Calendar Year 2027 Home Health Prospective Payment System rate update finalizes a temporary behavior adjustment along with recalibrated case-mix weights, updated functional impairment levels, comorbidity subgroups and low-utilization policy. The CY 2027 Physician Fee Schedule rule resets Part B payment and codifies the Medicare Prescription Drug Inflation Rebate Program. The Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program rule finalizes and codifies the negotiation program and new Part D policies required by the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022. A fourth document the same day corrects a typographical error in the 10/20/26 proposed rule implementing Sections 6219, 6220 and 6224 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026. Three of these are logged as lightly matched by monitored publishers; the correction is a confirmed gap. Read together, they are the price list for 2027 across the home visit, the office visit and the pharmacy counter, set in a single day of filings.

**Why it matters:** Home health is the setting older adults are moving into, 1,903.60 thousands of jobs in October 2026, up 4.4% year over year, and the HH PPS rule changes the case-mix and low-utilization math that decides which of those visits get paid for and at what level. The Part D and negotiation rules decide what a beneficiary hands over at the counter. None of that reaches a Medicare household as news; it reaches them as a 2027 bill or a changed plan of care. KFF's 11/07/26 analysis of the proposed 340B cut shows the same mechanism one level up: a payment change that moves revenue away from safety-net hospitals and toward for-profit hospitals without anyone voting on it.

**Why pitch this now:** The rules were published 11/09/26 and are final, not proposed, so the 2027 numbers they set are the numbers providers will build budgets and schedules against over the next six weeks. The correction to the 10/20/26 proposed rule shows that the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 implementation is still mid-stream and not yet locked.

**Angle:** Whether a household on Medicare can find out, from the rules as written, what changes for them in 2027, when the three documents that determine it published on one day and only in the Federal Register. Working title: "The Day Medicare Priced 2027." For home health and nonprofit provider executives planning the year, and for the families whose care plan those rules quietly rewrite.

- Medicare priced 2027 in a single day of filings
- The home health rule changes which visits get paid for
- Drug price negotiation is now in the rulebook, not just the law

**Potential outlets:**
- **LeadingAge** — its nonprofit home health, hospice and LTSS members have to turn the recalibrated case-mix weights and the temporary behavior adjustment into a 2027 budget.
- **Fierce Healthcare** — follows Part B and Part D rulemaking closely enough to want all three same-day finals read against each other.
- **Modern Healthcare** — can pair the Physician Fee Schedule rule with KFF's 340B finding on revenue moving from safety-net to for-profit hospitals.
- **Kiplinger** — translates negotiation and Part D codification into what a retiree actually pays next year.

**Drug price negotiation stops being a law and becomes a rulebook**
*Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program and Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program*  
- Angle: What the 11/09/26 final rule codifies about the negotiation program, Part D policy and fixed-combination drugs that are new formulations, written for people filling prescriptions under Part D.
- Hook: The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 authority is now finalized and codified in regulation rather than left to guidance.
- For readers: Pull your current Part D drug list and check which of your medications are fixed combination products, because the rule finalizes a specific policy for new formulations of those.
- For the trade: Plans and pharmacy operations teams need the codified Part D policies mapped before 2027 benefit administration locks.
- Why it matters: The difference between guidance and codified rule is how hard it is to change what you pay later.
- Also: Pairs naturally with the same-day Physician Fee Schedule rule, which codifies the Prescription Drug Inflation Rebate Program.
- Pitch to: Fierce Healthcare, Bankrate Retirement

**What your doctor gets paid in 2027 was decided this week**
*Medicare and Medicaid Programs; CY 2027 Payment Policies Under the Physician Fee Schedule and Other Changes to Part B Payment and Coverage Policies; Medicare Shared Savings Program Requirements; and Medicare Prescription Drug Inflation Rebate Program*  
- Angle: A walk through the CY 2027 Physician Fee Schedule final rule's Part B payment and coverage changes and Shared Savings Program requirements, for older patients who want to know whether their physician keeps seeing them.
- Hook: The rule is final as of 11/09/26 and also codifies the Medicare Prescription Drug Inflation Rebate Program.
- For readers: Ask at your next appointment whether the practice is staying in Medicare and in any Shared Savings arrangement for 2027, before you schedule January visits.
- For the trade: Groups in the Shared Savings Program have finalized requirements to reconcile with existing contracts and relative value changes.
- Why it matters: Losing a physician who stops taking Medicare costs you continuity that is hard to rebuild at 80.

*Medicare Cuts to 340B Drug Payments Will Hit Safety-Net Hospitals While Benefiting For-Profit Hospitals*  
- Angle: KFF's 11/07/26 analysis of the proposed Medicare 340B reimbursement cut and the offsetting increase for other outpatient services, read by patients who rely on a safety-net hospital for outpatient care.
- Hook: KFF finds the same policy reduces safety-net hospital revenue while increasing for-profit hospital revenue, and no monitored publisher matched it.
- For readers: If your outpatient infusions or specialty drugs come through a safety-net hospital, ask whether the program is staying open at its current hours next year.
- For the trade: Outpatient finance teams should model the 340B reduction and the other-services increase together rather than separately, since the net differs sharply by ownership type.
- Why it matters: The hospital that treats you without asking about your ability to pay may be the one absorbing the loss.
- Also: Confirmed gap; ownership-type split is the chart.
- Pitch to: Modern Healthcare, Fierce Healthcare
